content.text:
`/electron/init-oauth-proxy` now forwards each cookie from the inner sign-in response as its own `Set-Cookie` header, in the order the inner response emitted them. The change is in `packages/electron/src/routes.ts`. It reads the cookies with `getSetCookie()` and appends each one to the response headers.

I added a test in `packages/electron/test/electron.test.ts`. It mocks the global `fetch` to return a redirect URL plus the two cookies from your example. It checks for a `302` with a `Location` header and two separate `Set-Cookie` entries starting `first.cookie=one` and `second.cookie=two`. The new test passes, and the electron package typechecks with `tsc --noEmit`. I did not run the rest of the electron test file, `pnpm typecheck`, or the docs.

I didn't add tests for the other requirements. Cookie attributes are forwarded as the raw header strings, and the no-cookie case adds nothing to the headers. Neither case has a test of its own.

I had to run the shell commands with the sandbox disabled, because the sandbox failed to start (`bwrap: Can't mount proc`). Nothing is committed.
